title: Bounded-below objects detect isomorphisms in sheaf derived categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Work in its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Say $H$ is bounded below if $H^q(H)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $q$. If a morphism $\alpha:B\to G$ induces bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(H[n],B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H[n],G)$ for every bounded-below object $H$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. No boundedness hypothesis is imposed on $B$ or $G$.
